prompt:
Transform the raw CSV below. Output ONLY the transformed CSV file, including the header row, with no code fence and no extra text.

The transformation rules are authoritative:
1. Parse the input as comma-separated rows. A field is quoted only if, after optional leading spaces or tabs, it begins with `"`. Inside a quoted field, doubled quotes `""` become a literal `"`. A comma inside a quoted field never splits columns.
2. In a quoted field, remove the outer quotes, then ignore only spaces or tabs between the closing quote and the next comma or end of line.
3. In an unquoted field, a comma splits columns unless it is escaped as `\,`.
4. After parsing, decode escapes in every field from left to right: `\\` -> `\`, `\"` -> `"`, `\,` -> `,`. No other escapes are special.
5. In unquoted fields only, trim leading and trailing ASCII spaces and tabs.
6. In quoted fields, preserve all inner whitespace exactly; do not trim it.
7. Type inference applies only to unquoted fields. Quoted fields always remain strings, even if they look numeric or date-like.
8. In any unquoted column, the case-insensitive tokens empty, `null`, `nil`, `n/a`, and `na` become null.
9. In unquoted `ID` and `Age`, parse `[+-]?\d+` as integers.
10. In unquoted `Score`, parse `[+-]?\d+(?:\.\d+)?` as decimal numbers.
11. Render parsed decimals without exponent, without a leading `+`, and without unnecessary trailing zeros or a trailing decimal point.
12. In unquoted `Active`, map `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, and `0` case-insensitively to booleans.
13. In unquoted `Joined`, parse dates in exactly three formats: `YYYY-MM-DD`, `MM/DD/YYYY`, and `DD-Mon-YYYY` using English month abbreviations. Render parsed dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`.
14. Rename headers with this exact map: `ID->id`, `Name->full_name`, `Alias->nickname`, `Age->age`, `Score->score`, `Active->active`, `Joined->joined_date`, `City->city`, `Note->note`.
15. Output columns in this exact order: `id,full_name,nickname,age,score,active,joined_date,city,note`.
16. Remove duplicate data rows after full normalization, keeping only the first occurrence.
17. Sort normalized rows by `joined_date` ascending, then `id` ascending. Rows whose `joined_date` is null sort after all rows with a date. The sort must be stable.
18. Output serialization is exact: the header is unquoted; null renders as an empty field; booleans render as `true` or `false`; integers and decimals render unquoted; parsed dates render unquoted as `YYYY-MM-DD`; every string renders as a double-quoted CSV field with any inner `"` doubled.

difficulty_rationale: Quoted versus unquoted whitespace rules differ, so a single trim heuristic breaks multiple rows.
Escape decoding happens after CSV parsing, which punishes implementations that hand CSV parsing to a generic library and stop there.
Type inference is column-specific and unquoted-only, so quoted numeric-looking values must stay as strings.
Three date formats, stable sorting, and null-last sorting interact across many rows.
Duplicate elimination happens after full normalization, so raw duplicates and normalization-induced duplicates must both collapse.
Exact output formatting is brittle because all strings are always quoted while scalars are not.
Several rows share the same sort keys, so instability changes later lines even if normalization is otherwise correct.
Backslash-escaped commas in unquoted fields force a parser that understands both RFC-like quotes and custom escapes.
